items.title: A green graph is not a résumé — so we built a GitHub contribution filler you can undo
items.pt:
GitHub's contribution graph is a bad metric, and most developers know it. It still gets a glance: after a break, after a job in private repos, after a year that looks quieter than it felt.

The usual response is a script. Clone gitfiti or github-activity-generator, paste a personal token, wait, and hope the dates land on the right day. items.title: Why Your Side Project Has 0 Users (And Why It’s Not a Coding Problem)
items.pt:
I spent three months building the perfect API. It had clean architecture, 99% test coverage, and a beautiful CI/CD pipeline. I deployed it, leaned back in my chair, and waited for the users to roll in.

They didn't.

I got exactly 0 visitors. Not a single person signed up.

items.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
items.pt: Looped models have emerged as a prominent paradigm for reasoning, with successes on simple reasoning puzzles such as Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Unique. items.title: Quantifying structural stability of transparent models for general insurance pricing
items.pt: The short duration of general insurance contracts leads to rapid distributional shifts in the data, warranting regular model updates. items.title: FLEX-LBP: Learning Local Binary Patterns with Exact Binary Inference for Texture Classification
items.pt: Local Binary Patterns (LBP) remain among the most widely used texture descriptors, from industrial inspection to medical imaging. Yet their radius, sampling angles, color transform and thresholds are fixed by hand for each dataset. We present FLEX-LBP, which learns these parameters by backpropagation while every forward pass computes exact binary codes and hard histogram counts. A straight-through estimator acts only in the backward pass, so the deployed descriptor is an interpretable hard-binar
